system_prompt:
You are a careful, neutral coder of the REALIZED OUTCOME of a corporate transaction
over the 3-5 years AFTER it closed. You are given ONE evidence slice assembled from
public primary sources (financial filings, reputable press) that describes ONLY the
post-deal trajectory -- how the combined company actually fared. You are
DELIBERATELY NOT shown how the deal was structured at closing (what transferred and
what did not), and you must NOT speculate about the deal's structure. Code STRICTLY
the documented realized outcome. If the slice does not let you determine a field,
you MUST return "uncertain" -- never guess, never infer from outside knowledge.

Emit a single structured record with these fields.

C. FAILURE-PATHWAY INCIDENCE -- code strictly from the DOCUMENTED OUTCOME at the
3-5 year horizon. A pathway is a REALIZED DISRUPTION OVER TIME, not a structural
property of the deal.
  p4_pathway: Is there documented disruption specifically at the product/process
    interface (the acquired product could not be aligned with the operating
    processes over time; product-line/operations incoherence realized after the
    deal)? 1 = yes; 0 = no / none documented; uncertain.
  p5_pathway: Is there documented fracture specifically at the process/organization
    interface (operations vs people/management/culture; integration of operations
    broke against the organization over time)? 1 = yes; 0 = no / none documented;
    uncertain.
  t1_archetype: Is there documented incoherence in the controlling-intent archetype
    itself as it played out (e.g. an announced "merger of equals" that operated as
    one-sided dominance)? A channel SEPARATE from the product/process and
    process/organization pathways. 1 = yes; 0 = no; uncertain.
  t2_model: Is there documented incompatibility of the two business models
    (value-capture logics that could not be reconciled over time)? A channel
    SEPARATE from the pathways above. 1 = yes; 0 = no; uncertain.

D. performance_metric: the single best-documented post-deal outcome scalar in the
   slice (e.g. "divested 80.1% after ~108 months", "~$99bn goodwill write-down",
   "no divestiture; assets retained"). One short phrase. If none, "not documented".

rationale: 2-4 sentences citing the slice lines that drove your p4_pathway and
p5_pathway codes specifically. Cite ONLY realized-outcome evidence; do NOT reason
about how the deal was structured at closing.

Emit ONLY the structured record. Code conservatively: absence of documented
evidence for a pathway is 0 (not-documented); inability to determine is "uncertain".

# Outcome sub-dossier — Quality Care Properties, Inc. realized record after merger into Welltower Inc., ~3-5-year horizon

> EVIDENTIARY STANDARD: every factual line ends with a `[SRC: <SEC accession / URL>]`
> tag pointing to a public primary source. A fact that cannot be so sourced is written
> `[UNVERIFIED]` and is never guessed. Because QCP was merged whole into an acquirer
> subsidiary and deregistered, there is no post-closing public 10-K filed by QCP itself;
> the realized record for the entity is traced through its own deregistration filing and
> (where the acquirer separately discloses it) the acquirer's subsequent public filings
> and reputable press. This sub-dossier contains no information about how the
> transaction was structured at closing.

## Public-reporting status after the transaction (feasibility-relevant)
- QCP's last periodic annual report on Form 10-K on EDGAR covers fiscal year 2017 and was filed March 8, 2018, before the merger closed. [SRC: SEC EDGAR filing index for CIK 0001677203, https://www.sec.gov/cgi-bin/browse-edgar?action=getcompany&CIK=0001677203&type=10-K]
- QCP filed a Form 15-12B on August 6, 2018 to terminate the registration of its common stock and suspend its reporting obligations under the Securities Exchange Act of 1934. [SRC: SEC accession 0001104659-18-049804, Form 15-12B]
- QCP's EDGAR filing history contains no Form 10-K or Form 20-F filed after the Form 15-12B; no annual report or other periodic report exists on EDGAR for QCP as a standalone registrant covering any period after the merger, so no audited public financial statements exist for QCP specifically for the ~2021-2023 outcome window. [SRC: SEC EDGAR filing index for CIK 0001677203, https://www.sec.gov/cgi-bin/browse-edgar?action=getcompany&CIK=0001677203&type=10-K]

## Whether the acquirer separately discloses the acquired business
- Welltower's Form 10-K for the year ended December 31, 2021 does not report a distinct "Quality Care Properties" or "QCP" reporting segment; its only reference to Quality Care Properties is the Exhibit Index's incorporation by reference of the April 2018 Agreement and Plan of Merger. [SRC: SEC accession 0000766704-22-000013, Form 10-K, Exhibit Index]
- Welltower's Form 10-K for the year ended December 31, 2022 separately reports NOI concentration by "relationship," including a "ProMedica" relationship representing 10% of net operating income in 2022 (12% in 2021, 11% in 2020) and, for the Triple-net segment specifically, approximately 26% of Triple-net segment revenues and 4% of total revenues from ProMedica in 2022 — this is disclosure at the operator-relationship level, not a distinct former-QCP entity or segment. [SRC: SEC accession 0000766704-23-000010, Form 10-K, Item 7 MD&A]

## Realized record of the ProMedica operator relationship (portfolio/relationship level)
- In December 2022, ProMedica relinquished to Welltower its 15% interest in 147 skilled nursing facilities previously owned by the Welltower/ProMedica joint venture, in exchange for a lease modification that relieved ProMedica of its lease obligation on those 147 properties; the joint venture's remaining 58 assisted living and memory care properties continued to be operated by ProMedica under an amended lease, backed by the existing guaranty. [SRC: SEC accession 0000766704-23-000010, Form 10-K, Item 7 MD&A]
- Concurrently, Welltower and Integra Healthcare Properties ("Integra") entered into master leases covering the 147-facility skilled nursing portfolio, with approximately 15 regional operators expected to sublease from Integra to operate the properties; in December 2022 and January 2023 Welltower sold Integra a 15% ownership interest in 85 of those facilities, with Integra expected to acquire an interest in the remaining 62 assets during 2023. [SRC: SEC accession 0000766704-23-000010, Form 10-K, Item 7 MD&A]
- Reputable press corroborates the same operator transition, describing it as the formation of a joint venture between Welltower and Integra Health and a plan to transition skilled nursing assets then operated by ProMedica. [SRC: https://welltower.investorroom.com/2022-11-07-Welltower-Announces-the-Formation-of-Joint-Venture-with-Integra-Health-and-Plan-to-Transition-Skilled-Nursing-Assets-Currently-Operated-by-ProMedica]

## Items noted but not primary-verifiable
- Welltower's FY2022 Form 10-K does not itself state the extent to which the 147 skilled nursing facilities held in "the Welltower/ProMedica joint venture" as of December 2022 correspond to, are a subset of, or overlap with the specific real estate portfolio QCP owned immediately before the 2018 merger; a precise asset-level reconciliation between the entities is [UNVERIFIED] from the documents reviewed for this dossier.

## Outcome summary (realized record only)
- Because QCP was merged whole into a Welltower acquisition subsidiary and deregistered from SEC reporting in August 2018, no separate public 3-5-year financial record exists for QCP as a standalone entity, and Welltower's subsequent Form 10-K filings do not report a distinct former-QCP segment; the entity-level outcome is therefore not publicly observable and is coded as such rather than inferred from Welltower's consolidated results. [SRC: SEC accession 0001104659-18-049804, Form 15-12B] [SRC: SEC accession 0000766704-22-000013, Form 10-K]
- At the operator-relationship level, Welltower's own FY2022 Form 10-K separately discloses that the ProMedica-related joint venture holding the post-acute/skilled-nursing real estate underwent a documented operator transition in December 2022/January 2023: 147 skilled nursing facilities moved from ProMedica's operation to Integra Healthcare Properties and roughly 15 regional sub-operators, while 58 assisted living/memory-care properties in the same joint venture remained with ProMedica. [SRC: SEC accession 0000766704-23-000010, Form 10-K, Item 7 MD&A]

[SLICE END]

  "rationale": "The provided slice indicates that QCP was deregistered and its entity-level outcome is not publicly observable in the acquirer's filings. There is no documented evidence of product/process incoherence or process/organization fracture."
}
